facts.statement: Cumberland recorded 9,540 premises delivered.
North Yorkshire recorded 9,170 premises delivered.
Westmorland and Furness recorded 8,560 premises delivered.
East Riding of Yorkshire recorded 7,420 premises delivered.
Highland recorded 6,760 premises delivered.
Cornwall recorded 6,220 premises delivered.
Wiltshire recorded 5,830 premises delivered.
Dorset recorded 4,220 premises delivered.
East Lindsey recorded 4,090 premises delivered.
West Suffolk recorded 3,940 premises delivered.
Urban areas accounted for 9% of annual BDUK delivery.
Rural delivery represented between 85% and 92% of annual delivery across the reported period.
An estimated 43,880 delivered premises previously lacked superfast broadband of at least 30 Mbit/s.
Those premises represented 23% of annual delivery.
The BDUK address checker covers England and Wales.
The checker reports whether gigabit broadband is available or planned for an address.
Checker data is drawn from the January Open Market Review.
The January OMR data used by the checker was published in June 2026.
The checker was scheduled for its next data update in September 2026.
The checker is expected to update every four months thereafter.
Supplier delivery-plan changes can make checker information change.
BDUK does not guarantee complete address-level accuracy for checker status.
Defra's July 2026 findings state that broadband availability in the most rural areas trails the rest of England.
Defra reports proportionally more mobile not-spots in majority-rural constituencies than in less-rural constituencies.
